scenario.title: Stale backfill overwrites a newer user update
scenario.description: A background job copies legacy_name into display_name while the new application lets users set display_name.
scenario.requirement: A backfill must not overwrite a committed, explicitly supplied user display name.
assumptions: update_display_name is the only source of explicitly user-supplied display names.

buggy.backfill.py:
"""Populates display_name for existing profiles, one row per transaction."""

SELECT_BATCH = "SELECT id, legacy_name FROM profiles WHERE display_name IS NULL ORDER BY id LIMIT %(limit)s"


def backfill_display_names(conn, limit):
    with conn.transaction():
        rows = conn.execute(SELECT_BATCH, {"limit": limit}).fetchall()
    for row in rows:
        with conn.transaction():
            conn.execute(
                "UPDATE profiles SET display_name = %(display_name)s WHERE id = %(id)s",
                {"display_name": row["legacy_name"], "id": row["id"]},
            )

files.corrected_backfill:
"""Populates display_name for existing profiles, one row per transaction."""

SELECT_BATCH = "SELECT id, legacy_name FROM profiles WHERE display_name IS NULL ORDER BY id LIMIT %(limit)s"


def backfill_display_names(conn, limit):
    with conn.transaction():
        rows = conn.execute(SELECT_BATCH, {"limit": limit}).fetchall()
    for row in rows:
        with conn.transaction():
            conn.execute(
                "UPDATE profiles SET display_name = %(display_name)s WHERE id = %(id)s AND display_name IS NULL",
                {"display_name": row["legacy_name"], "id": row["id"]},
            )

conflict.risk_explanation: Backfill SELECTs rows WHERE display_name IS NULL in one transaction then UPDATEs SET display_name by id in a later transaction without re-checking IS NULL. A concurrent app_v2 UPDATE setting display_name between SELECT and UPDATE is blindly overwritten with stale legacy_name, a lost update.

proposal.name: backfill_blind_overwrite_loses_v2_write
proposal.rationale: Backfill SELECTs the NULL row then blind UPDATEs display_name by id. If v2 sets display_name between SELECT and UPDATE, the stale backfill UPDATE wins and loses v2 write. Serially v2 always wins, so final must be v2 value.

invariants.description: display_name for id 1 should remain the concurrent v2 value; a correct backfill must not overwrite a non-NULL concurrent write
